title: 449. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Composing Trigonometric Graph Transformations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Vertical stretch with a vertical shift
questions.learningObjective: Read the amplitude and midline of a sine with two vertical transformations.
questions.question: What are the amplitude and midline of \(y=2\sin x+1\)?
questions.explanation: In \(y=A\sin x+D\), the coefficient \(A=2\) is the amplitude and the constant \(D=1\) gives the midline \(y=1\). The graph oscillates between \(-1\) and \(3\). Exchanging the two numbers describes \(y=\sin x+2\).
questions.hint: The factor multiplying the sine controls the amplitude; the added constant controls the midline.

questions.concept: Horizontal compression with a vertical shift
questions.learningObjective: Describe a combination of a period change and a vertical shift.
questions.question: How is the graph of \(y=\sin(2x)+3\) related to the graph of \(y=\sin x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Its period is halved to \(\pi\), and it is shifted \(3\) units up.

options.label: B
options.text: Its period is doubled to \(4\pi\), and it is shifted \(3\) units up.

questions.explanation: The coefficient \(2\) inside the sine compresses the graph horizontally, giving period \(\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi\). The constant \(3\) outside raises the graph by \(3\). A coefficient greater than \(1\) inside shortens the period; it does not lengthen it.

questions.concept: Reading period and phase shift from factored form
questions.learningObjective: Read the period and the phase shift from a sinusoidal rule in factored form.
questions.question: What are the period and the phase shift of \(y=3\sin\left(2\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)-1\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Period \(\pi\) and a shift of \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) to the right

options.label: B
options.text: Period \(2\pi\) and a shift of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) to the right

questions.explanation: In the form \(y=A\sin\left(B(x-h)\right)+k\), the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi\) and the phase shift is \(h=\frac{\pi}{4}\) to the right. The rule is already factored, so the shift is read directly; multiplying \(h\) by \(B\) gives the incorrect \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).
questions.hint: When the coefficient of \(x\) is already factored out, the shift is the number subtracted from \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Find the range of a cosine with a reflection, a stretch, and a vertical shift.
questions.question: What is the range of \(y=-2\cos(x+\pi)+4\)?
questions.explanation: The cosine factor takes all values from \(-1\) to \(1\), so \(-2\cos(x+\pi)\) takes all values from \(-2\) to \(2\). Adding \(4\) gives the range \(2\le y\le 6\). The reflection and the horizontal shift do not change the range; the interval from \(-2\) to \(2\) ignores the vertical shift.
questions.hint: Only the amplitude and the vertical shift affect the range.

questions.concept: Order of a shift and a stretch
questions.learningObjective: Apply a vertical shift followed by a vertical stretch in the stated order.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\sin x\) is first shifted \(2\) units up, and the result is then stretched vertically by a factor of \(3\) away from the \(x\)-axis. Which rule describes the final graph?
questions.explanation: After the shift the rule is \(y=\sin x+2\). Stretching vertically by \(3\) multiplies the whole expression by \(3\): \(y=3(\sin x+2)=3\sin x+6\). The rule \(y=3\sin x+2\) results from stretching first and shifting afterwards; the order matters.
questions.hint: Apply each transformation to the entire current rule, in the order stated.

questions.concept: Compression followed by a horizontal shift
questions.learningObjective: Compose a horizontal compression with a horizontal shift in the stated order.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\sin x\) is first compressed horizontally by a factor of \(2\), giving \(y=\sin 2x\), and the result is then shifted \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) units to the right. Which rule describes the final graph?
questions.explanation: A shift of \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) to the right replaces \(x\) by \(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\) in \(y=\sin 2x\): \(y=\sin\left(2\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)=\sin\left(2x-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\). The rule \(y=\sin\left(2x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\) is shifted only \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) to the right.
questions.hint: Replace \(x\) by \(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\) everywhere, then distribute the coefficient \(2\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a fully transformed sine function at a given point.
questions.question: What is the value of \(y=2\sin\left(3x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+1\) at \(x=\frac{\pi}{3}\)?
questions.explanation: The argument is \(3\cdot\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{2}=\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}\). Then \(y=2\sin\frac{\pi}{2}+1=2\cdot 1+1=3\). The value \(-1\) would arise from an argument of \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\), which results from a sign error.
questions.hint: Compute the argument of the sine first, then evaluate and apply the outside operations.

questions.concept: Maximum of a reflected and shifted sine
questions.learningObjective: Find the maximum value of a sine with a negative coefficient and a vertical shift.
questions.question: What is the maximum value of \(y=-4\sin(2x)+1\)?
questions.explanation: The amplitude is \(|-4|=4\) and the midline is \(y=1\), so the maximum is \(1+4=5\); it occurs where \(\sin 2x=-1\). The value \(-3=1-4\) is the minimum of the function.
questions.hint: The maximum is the midline value plus the amplitude, whatever the sign of the coefficient.

questions.concept: Writing a rule from four features
questions.learningObjective: Write a sine rule from amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline.
questions.question: A sine graph has amplitude \(2\), period \(\pi\), midline \(y=1\), and is shifted \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) units to the right relative to \(y=2\sin 2x+1\). Which rule describes it?
questions.explanation: The period \(\pi\) gives \(B=2\). A shift of \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) to the right replaces \(x\) by \(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\), giving \(y=2\sin\left(2\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)+1=2\sin\left(2x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+1\). The rule with \(2x-\frac{\pi}{6}\) is shifted only \(\frac{\pi}{12}\) to the right.
questions.hint: The shift must be applied to \(x\) itself, inside the factor \(B\).

questions.concept: First maximum of a transformed sine
questions.learningObjective: Locate the first maximum of a transformed sine for non-negative values of the variable.
questions.question: For \(x\ge 0\), what is the smallest value of \(x\) at which \(y=3\sin\left(2x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+2\) reaches its maximum?
questions.explanation: The maximum occurs when the sine equals \(1\), that is, when \(2x-\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi\). For \(k=0\), \(2x=\frac{5\pi}{6}\) and \(x=\frac{5\pi}{12}\); for \(k=-1\) the value of \(x\) is negative. The value \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) is \(2x\), before dividing by \(2\).
questions.hint: Set the argument equal to \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and solve for \(x\), dividing every term by \(2\).
